subject: english
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. 

I asked my friend / where had he / learnt to dance / so well.
solution:
The erroneous part is **"where had he"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the usage of "where had he" is incorrect instead of this we need to use "where he had"
 
• According to grammar, whenever we need to use an interrogative sentence then, we need to use the modal verb before the subject and whenever we need to write a simple sentence then, we need to write a modal verb after the subject.
 
• Let's see an example-
 
 
• Interrogative sentence- Where did you plan to sleep tonight?
 
• Simple sentence- I'll show you where you can sleep.
 
 

**So the correct sentence is-** *I asked my friend **where he had **learnt to dance so well.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__***

 
• There is a difference between learned and learnt. The verb forms are learn→ learnt→ learnt
 
• "Learnt" is a past participle form of Learn {The verb forms are learn→ learnt→ learnt} and "Learned" is an adjective i.e. means gain or acquire knowledge of or skill in (something) by study, experience, or being taught.
 
• Let's see some examples-
 
 
• I **have learnt** a lot in the seven weeks.
 
• This sort of aggression is **learned behavior. (learned is an adjective here)**
 
 
 
• **There is also a difference of British English and American English between both the words.**
